"''It is of no concern.|[[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] and [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]]|{{Film|VI}}}} '''Sullust''' was the primary [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of the [[Sullust system/Legends|Sullust system]], located in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] at the conjuncture of the [[Rimma Trade Route/Legends|Rimma Trade Route]] and the [[Silvestri Trace]]. It was the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Sullustan/Legends|Sullustans]]. ==Description== {{Quote|Sullust shines as a nova of capitalism.|[[Shu Mai/Legends|Shu Mai]]|{{HoloNetNewsWeb|46|regional/1337_1.html|Sullustans Elect President}}}} [[File:DiabDuin-TOR.png|thumb|left|150px|[[Diab Duin]], a politician from Sullust]] Sullust was a terrestrial [[Planet/Legends|planet]] that occupied the fourth [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] from the [[Star/Legends|star]] [[Sullust (star)|Sullust]] in the [[Sullust system/Legends|Sullust system]] in the [[Brema sector/Legends|Brema sector]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] region of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. Situated on the [[Rimma Trade Route/Legends|Rimma Trade Route]] and within the area known as the [[Trailing Sectors/Legends|Trailing Sectors]], Sullust had standard [[Gravity/Legends|gravity]] and possessed two [[Moon/Legends|moons]]: a large planetoid named [[Sulon/Legends|Sulon]] and an unremarkable hunk of rock named [[Umnub]]. Sullust's day lasted 20 [[Standard hour/Legends|standard hours]] and its year lasted 263 [[Standard day/Legends|standard days]]. The planet was 12,780 [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]] in diameter and featured terrain including mountains, volcanoes, rocky deserts, and caves; multicolored rock veined by channels of [[Magma/Legends|magma]] covered Sullust's entire surface. The [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] of Sullust was barely breathable, with hot and thick clouds of toxic gases released in volcanic eruptions rendering the planet's surface lethal for sustained habitation and uncomfortable for short visits. Atmospheric blackouts occurred on a regular basis due to large gouts of smoky ash. Its surface was also dangerously volatile; while Sullust's geology was poorly understood, the mantle between the planet's core and its thick crust appeared to be semipermeable, allowing eruptions to occur frequently. Most of the opaque substances ejected by the volcanoes remained in the upper atmosphere while heavier gases flowed back down, resulting in high surface visibility and noxious surface air. Sullust was popularly known as "the volcano planet," but only certain portions of the world contained active volcanoes. Few of the volcanoes were reliably extinct, however. The [[Sullustan/Legends|Sullustan]] [[Species/Legends|species]] evolved in the more hospitable underground of the planet, where a stable system of tunnels connected edible [[Lichen/Legends|lichen]] gardens to pools of potable [[Water/Legends|water]]. A hub of trade along the Rimma Trade Route, Sullust had a corporate system of government and exported [[Starship/Legends|starships]], [[Computer/Legends|computers]], [[Droid/Legends|droids]], [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] technology, and astrogation technology while importing foodstuffs and water. During the reign of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] there were many bases built on the planet, and several major cities were locked down by Imperials. ==History== The planet joined the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] when Sullustan merchants connected their planet to [[Tapani sector/Legends|Tapani sector]] with the Rimma Trade Route in [[5500 BBY/Legends|5500 BBY]]. Sullust became a major hub of trade soon after it achieved contact with the rest of the galaxy, and the presence of corporations and manufacturing on the world increased as galactic commerce became more common there.''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Saga Edition Core Rulebook]]'' The [[SoroSuub Corporation/Legends|SoroSuub Corporation]] was already a part of Sullust's economy and government when the planet first gained access to interstellar travel, and over [[Time/Legends|time]], SoroSuub aided Sullust's government while becoming increasingly influential in the diplomacy of Sullust. Sullust was an honored member of the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]]. It was attacked by the [[Krath/Legends|Krath]] during the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]], but was successfully defended by the Galactic Republic. The world was volatile with hundreds of active volcanoes, producing a noxious, toxic [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] and intense electrical storms. These conditions, combined with the planet's rich mineral deposits, caused the native Sullustan inhabitants to live in underground caves. The underground caves were humid and cool, with a diverse biosphere supported by underground lakes. The planet was once known for its podraces. During the [[New Sith Wars]], the [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]] [[Battle of Sullust (New Sith Wars)|captured]] the planet.
[[File:BattleOfSullustSystem_Nightsisters.png|thumb|left|240px|A battle over Sullust during the Clone Wars.]]
Sullust was the headquarters of the [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]-spanning SoroSuub Corporation, a member of the [[Commerce Guild/Legends|Commerce Guild]]. Nearly one-half of the population was under its employment. As the Old Republic crumbled, the governing [[Sullustan Council]] became weak. Under President [[Beolars Bribbs/Legends|Beolars Bribbs]] who was also the Galactic [[Senator/Legends|Senator]], the planet seceded from the Republic in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]] and joined the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]]. Less than a month later the Republic dispatched a task force to retake the planet, led by [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Rees Alrix]]. The Republic took heavy casualties in the [[Battle of Sullust (Republic traitor)|battle]] due to a treachery in their midst and the planet remained one of the Confederacy's most prized holdings until the end of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].''[[The Clone Wars Campaign Guide]]'' With the expansion of [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] [[New Order/Legends|New Order]], SoroSuub assumed leadership of Sullust with [[Corporate Proclamation 137d]] and announced its full support of the Empire. In exchange for several lucrative contracts and the promise of guaranteed future business, SoroSuub took a hardline against the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] and its supporters. Angered at SoroSuub's illegal takeover and support of the Empire, Sullustans formed [[Sullustan Resistance|resistance cells]] under the leadership of [[Sian Tevv/Legends|Sian Tevv]] that became model rebel cells during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. Tevv's resistance fighters, combined with a coup to take over SoroSuub by pro-Alliance forces, garnered enough support to wrestle control of Sullust away from SoroSuub shortly before [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]]. Several [[Standard month/Legends|months]] after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]] launched a [[Raid on Sullust|strike]] to destroy a [[Capacitor (Sullust)|Capacitor]].[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (video game)|''Star Wars: Rogue Squadron'']] [[File:LavaRideOnSullust.jpg|thumb|left|180px|A lava flow on Sullust]] The Sullustan resistance remained independent from the Alliance, although it allowed the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Alliance Fleet]] to use Sullust as the staging point for planned destruction of the [[Death Star II/Legends|Death Star II]], since Sullust was an endpoint of the [[Sanctuary Pipeline/Legends|Sanctuary Pipeline]] as well as due to a board chairman of SoroSuub being rescued from Imperial detention by Rebel force. The Alliance also launched a [[Battle of Sullust (4 ABY)|diversionary attack]] in the system, to draw the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial fleet]] away from [[Endor/Legends|Endor]].''[[Star Wars Battlefront: Renegade Squadron]]'' After the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], Sullust was one of the first worlds to officially align itself with the [[Alliance of Free Planets]], and subsequently the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]. It was represented on the [[New Republic Provisional Council]] by [[Sian Tevv/Legends|Sian Tevv]] and later in the [[New Republic Senate/Legends|New Republic Senate]] by [[Niuk Niuv]] during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]]. Sullust went on to be a key member of the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]]. In [[5 ABY/Legends|5 ABY]], [[Superior General]] [[Sander Delvardus]] of the neighboring [[Eriadu Authority]] tried to conquer Sullust but he was [[Battle of Sullust (Delvardus campaign)|defeated]] by [[Sien Sovv]] who launched a counterattack campaign that liberated all the Authority. [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire]] took control over Sullust after the end of the [[Sith–Imperial War]]. SoroSuub was forced to keep at least 80% of its production facilities manufacturing Imperial vessels, most of which were not even of Sorosuub design. Forced into desperation, Sullustans began building secret underground facilities closer to the planet's core. Products created in those facilities were secretly smuggled offworld and sold in open market.''[[Legacy Era Campaign Guide]]'' ==Behind the scenes== The name Sullust first appeared (spelt Sullest) in the [[Adventures of the Starkiller, Episode I: The Star Wars|second draft]] of the script for [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''A New Hope'']], as part of the name of the [[Bomerwrights of Sullest]], crafters of [[Lightsaber/Legends|laser swords]].{{WebCite|url=https://www.starwarz.com/starkiller/adventures-of-the-starkiller-second-draft|text=Adventures of the Starkiller, Episode I: The Star Wars|archivedate=20240818175509}} In the [[The Star Wars: From The Adventures of Luke Starkiller|third draft]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Ben Kenobi]] still referenced Sullust, along with the planet [[Aquilae (The Star Wars)|Aquilae]],{{WebCite|url=https://www.starwarz.com/starkiller/the-star-wars-from-the-adventures-of-luke-starkiller-third-draft|text=The Star Wars: From The Adventures of Luke Starkiller|archivedate=20240818094359}} but [[George Lucas]] cut this line when writing the fourth draft.{{WebCite|url=https://www.starwarz.com/starkiller/star-wars-the-adventures-of-luke-starkiller-as-taken-from-the-journal-of-the-whills|text=''The Adventures of Luke Starkiller as taken from the Journal of the Whills: Saga I: The Star Wars'', fourth draft|archivedate=20240518135003}} Nonetheless, Lucas asked [[Mark Hamill]] to memorize this line of dialogue.''[[The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film]]''{{YouTube|video=rihbi2U7tNg|text=Mark Hamill on the one line he begged George Lucas to take out of Star Wars|channel=lostinhistorychannel|name=Lost in History}} The PC game [[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|''Star Wars: Rebellion'']] and ''[[Star Wars: Rebellion: Prima's Official Strategy Guide]]'' mistakenly place Sullust in the [[Sluis sector/Legends|Sluis sector]] of the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]]. The Sluis sector is actually located in the Outer Rim. Moreover, ''Star Wars: Rebellion: Prima's Official Strategy Guide'' misspells the planet as "'''Sulust'''." Additionally, ''Rebellion''{{'s}} in-game encyclopedia entry for Sullust mistakenly states that the Sullust system openly threw their support to the Rebel Alliance after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. Rather, the Sullustan resistance movement merely provided independent support and aid, while many others remained hesitant to become involved, or still remained pro-Imperial. In the revised [[Star Wars: Episode I The Beginning|rough draft]] of the script for [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''The Phantom Menace'']], [[Clegg Holdfast/Legends|Clegg Holdfast]] is said to be from Sullust.{{DB|organization|boontapodrace|Boonta Eve Classic Podracers}} In ''[[Star Wars Battlefront: Renegade Squadron]]'' the planet is seen much differently.
